issues.legal_issue: Income received by managers of a Muslim religious endowment for distribution to beneficiaries in definite shares is assessable under the representative-income provision even if the managers are alleged to hold the property in their own right.
material_facts: A religious endowment’s income was used first to meet the endowment’s expenses, and the surplus was distributed among beneficiaries in definite shares.
The endowment’s managers prepared an annual list allocating the surplus to the beneficiaries and paid it to them.
The tax authorities assessed the surplus in the managing trustee’s hands as income of an association of persons; the dispute concerned whether section 41 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 applied.
issues.conclusion: Section 41 applied. The managers were entitled to receive the surplus on behalf of the beneficiaries, and it was assessable in their hands in the manner and to the extent it would be assessable on the beneficiaries.
issues.legal_principle: Section 41 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 applies where a person within its specified categories receives income on behalf of another. Technical vesting of property is not decisive: the persons covered by the section may hold property or merely manage it, and are treated as receiving income for others when they have no beneficial interest in it. A mutawalli of a Muslim wakf is a manager, not a trustee in the English-law sense. The Court relied on Vidya Varuthi Thirtha v. Balusami Ayyar, (1921) 48 I.A. 302, and Allah Rakhi v. Mohammad Abdur Rahim, (1933) 61 I.A. 50.

rule.if: income_tax_assessment_of_managed_income and manager_receives_income_for_others and manager_has_no_beneficial_interest and beneficiaries_have_definite_shares

predicates.income_tax_assessment_of_managed_income: A tax assessment concerns income collected or held by a person who manages property for others.
predicates.manager_receives_income_for_others: The person managing the property receives or holds its income for the benefit of other persons.
predicates.manager_has_no_beneficial_interest: The manager has no beneficial interest in the income that is collected or held.
predicates.beneficiaries_have_definite_shares: The persons for whose benefit the income is held are entitled to ascertainable shares of it.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment concerns managed income received for others by a manager with no beneficial interest, and the beneficiaries have definite shares, the manager is taxed as their representative.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme that vests management and administration of endowment property in managers, without clearly vesting the property itself, does not make the managers owners of that property.
material_facts: A court-approved scheme placed the management and administration of the endowment and its properties in a board of hereditary managers.
The scheme’s wording vested management and administration in the managers, rather than expressly vesting the properties themselves in them.
The tax authority argued that the scheme made the managers property-holders who received income in their own right.
issues.conclusion: The scheme vested management and administration, not the properties, in the managers; the managers therefore received the income on behalf of others.
issues.legal_principle: The scheme must be read according to its language, and clear wording is required before it can be taken to introduce a trust concept that alters the applicable principles of Muslim law. In that context, a mutawalli is a manager, and wakf property vests in God Almighty rather than in the mutawalli. The Court relied on Vidya Varuthi Thirtha v. Balusami Ayyar, (1921) 48 I.A. 302, and Allah Rakhi v. Mohammad Abdur Rahim, (1933) 61 I.A. 50.

predicates.court_scheme_interpretation: A court must determine what rights a management scheme gives to the persons managing endowed property.
predicates.scheme_vests_management_only: The scheme expressly places management and administration of the property in the managers.
predicates.scheme_does_not_clearly_vest_property: The scheme does not clearly state that the property itself is vested in the managers.

issues.definition: When a court interprets a scheme that vests management in managers but does not clearly vest the property in them, the scheme is construed as vesting management rather than property.
